Question: How does it feel to meet a friend after a long time?
Answer: To everyone thinking this is all very linear with both friends being elated at the first sight of each other and they begin hugging and shaking hands, no it isnt. Atleast for sudden appearances in public. When you see a friend in public after a long time, the first thing you feel in your nerves is anxiousness. You stroll around a bit among the crowd, with your head sprouting around quite akin to an Ostrich’s. You try to take sneaky glances at their face, like a DSLR taking on eight shots of the same frame per second, all in bid to secure the hunch that it is your friend that you have seen and not someone else. Slowly, yet quite surely the thoughts of whether your friend would remember you and the bond both of you had, hits your thoughts. You begin bargaining with yourself, if introducing yourself would bring a warm reaction or a nuanced glance. All while you get bogged in thoughts of how should you let them know of your presence, your own insecurities they finally turn around, looking towards you. It is at this moment, you raise your arm up, somewhat hesitatingly, against the will of every nerve that tells you “dont!” Along comes a warm smile in reply. They make their way among the crowd towards you, and suddenly, all of your stacked anxiety melts down in so much of just happiness and remembrance. Maybe this is how it is for some of us, meeting friends after long. Do let me know of your experiences in the comments. LOKI

Question: How do I use thyristors?
Answer: Thyristors are versatile semiconductor devices that are quite simple yet surprisingly powerful. Let me try to break down what they can do and how you can unleash theiir abilities in various practical applications. From dimming the lights in our homes to regulating large motors, thyristors are the unsung heroes behind the scenes in vast areas of electric circuit control. Their magic lies in one unique property — once turned on, they stay on until the thyristor is manually shut off. This on-off-on ability through Gate trigger signals makes them ideal for switching large loads such as those found in appliance regulators and elevators. Here is a drawing of the diagram and basic construction of a thyristor. One needs to simply supply a voltage pulse at the Gate terminal of the thyristor to flip its internal switch from blocking to conducting vast currents. The on/off switching speed can be finely tuned through gate trigger timing. By carefully varying the pulse width, we can effectively control the amount of voltage passing through. One could make light lamp dimmer by connecting a thyristor to an AC line, then flick its gate on and off at different pulse rates to give lower light intensities. Connected to sensors, they can convert real world variables like temperature, pressure or flow directly into electrical switching states to run appliances. LOKI Image credit: Pinterest

Answer: WALLED CITIES I wondered; wherein were the masons— grazed my fingers upon, those decaying walls, of your city— ghost quiet, decanted of time’s venom. The dust encamps on the roads; Footprints erased off the mud. door perished by termites— wherein someday, you lay imprisoned. Question: Story for The First Rendition (Contest Only).
Answer: CHRYSANTHEMUMS OF WINTER I stood on the grass, ruffling my hands on the almost barren chrysanthemum tree, waiting for her. It is only a few more minutes away, the moment I keep coming back to, year after year for almost a decade now. An incident flashes over me, so very fresh in my mortal cells. An excerpt from the winter, when I had the chance to take her out. I had presumed she too, like all the girls I had dated before, must be fond of roses. With the day already pre-planned in my diary of daydreaming, I spent months organizing the most perfect date I could attend. From my hairstyle, to what I was going to wear. From where we shall meet to wherein lies the best cuisine of the town. And yes, from where I shall buy those roses to greet her with. The fateful day arrived, with only misery written on my fortune. Bedridden, with high fever and typhoid, all the dreams of my beautifully crafted world fell apart, piece by piece. The bathroom was the only entity I was entitled to date, and medicines were the only kisses I was served by two strict, yet caring eyes of my mother. I had been lamenting and cursing my luck when there was a ring on our doorbell. It was her. Within a few minutes, she was there, postured beside my bed with one of her palms checking the temperature of my forehead. On the table, lay a Chrysanthemum flower. “These beautiful Chrysanthemums, do they survive these harsh winters?” I had asked. “Yes, I love them, and care for them, in return they bloom for me, even in winter.” “And if they don't?” “Then I ruffle their barren branches and wait for the melody of summer to arrive” Those days of my illness were perhaps the most special dates I ever had. We exchanged letters, which slowly became love letters. The day I was back at university, we kissed for the first time. Ever since she never left my hand…. . I pull my shawl closer, tighter over my, now-tattered Kurta. It has so much of her smell, the imprints of her heart smeared all over it. My smartphone rings out. It is past twelve. I placed the Chrysanthemum bouquet by the tombstone with a small note I wrote her this year. “Another year has passed, these winters, they shall never be the same again” Those were the winters of ‘71. Looking into the locket of our love, I mutter to myself “You are still with me, aren't you?”….. LOKI

Question: Can you write something dark and deep?
Answer: Her feet tumbled on the cold stone floor. One's gaze could easily get lost here. This room filled with dense mist, yet so very familiar to her. The air is cold and spiny, piercing her soul every time she breathes into it. The mist so very thick, and smelling of rotten carcass clogs her eyes and her nose, making her wince in the torment it does to her senses. She knows this story to her heart by now. After all, it has played out so many times before her eyes. She knew this twisted act of misery has preyed on her mind for many nights now. Orchestrated by someone or something she had never known of. She has become like the used cork of a bottle on the brink to be thrown away each time only to be chained in this prison of misery to be tormented and filled with dread, again and again. When did this all ever began? She does not know. All she ever remembers of a normal night was many many months ago. Neither does she know how this started or what this was. Is this her dream? If yes, why does it feel so real every time? And, the most harrowing sign of it was her sudden illness, ever since this started. She has been halved, the beautiful frame of her body reduced to a pale, bone-framed scaffolding, unrecognizable even to her own self. "You don't scare me, you filthy creature!" she shouts at one of the mirrors in front of her. Mirrors, mirrors all around, endless, fathomless. Her false bravado striking out with ferocity at them. The air seems still, suffocating her out in this endless prison of dread. Drops of sweat filtering down her curls, she rotates her fear-plagued eyes across the room, looking for any sign or movement. And then in an instance as if, the violin starts to play again, music of the abyss. A moment of dread flashes across her eyes. Not that wail of misery again. She prays for herself inside, knowing very well the torment that music brings along with its harrowing demeanor. The frequency gets higher every second and begins bouncing off the endless void of the room into her ears. "No...No...No...Naaa...Naaa" her hands covering her ears as to searching for relief from the piercing music that drills through her head. Her helpless cries, only elevates the misery wail, as they seemingly get lost somewhere endless. It is this that she fears the most, the endlessness of this prison that she seems to be caged in, this lack of any conclusive act makes her wonder if this is only a nightmare after all. What she sees next, baffles her own eyes. Her reflection, her very own reflection is slowly turning into a hideous monster in every mirror of the room. This was something that had never happened before. Her pale lips move, but there is no voice. Her shock clear on her face, mazed by the lines which seemed to be of a very old lady. But she was only seventeen! She has always thought this to be a repetitive nightmare, why then is it being different from before today? "WHO ARE YOU?? You dont..scare me" Her flickering eyes trying to restrain themselves of the fear that is haunting her inside. The monster is no one but she herself, but...but it can't be her. Sharp teeth, glistening of bloodlust, deep hideous red eyes. She cowers lower to the floor the music of the violin still revolting through her senses. The wail is finally getting to her. Despite all her tries to stop it from reaching her ears, she has failed. In anger and disgust, tears fill her eyes. With clenched fists, she hardens her jawbones for another cry towards the demoness. "You are not me! You demon! Don't meddle with my mind like this" She shrieks out again and again, her cries smelling of mercy pleadings. Warm tears rolled down her cheeks. Perhaps her tears were the only abode of warmth in this cold room of what seemed to be death's kingdom. The demoness in the reflection smiles, her crooked blood-stained teeth imparting every single second. "YOU FILTH!" She rushes to the mirror in front of her and bangs into it with both her hands. The glass cracks and shatters onto the floor on the impact of her pale bony fingers. A descent into madness, her eyes widen as she notices the trail of blood across her palms, deep cuts from the broken glass. But..but the demoness is still there, in every other mirror of this endless void, and her face...her face glistening among the broken glass she holds in her hands. The monstrous distortion of herself seemed to laugh at her misery. "No...No you can't be me" she grasps her throat as she falls to her knees, the ordeal making her senses numb. For the first time in her appearance, the demoness speaks, her voice metallic, and rough. "I am your truth Martha" she laughs again, the prominent blue veins of her face pulling through the skin. Martha's blood turned to ice in her veins. How does the demoness know her name? "How...how do you know my name?" Martha shouts. There is no response. There was she, seemingly still in the frame with a bloodthirsty smile. It seems so much of just an image, a distorted image of her face, hideously painted by the devil himself. Who would say this was the image that was so lively speaking to her just a few moments ago? Martha could not take it anymore. Her head hurt. With her black gown pulled up, she ran, side-stepping the mirrors with the demoness still smiling. Fearfully glancing back at the mirrors with dread, her mind raced with urgency. Bringing in the longest strides her frailing legs could cope up with. Not for long, the music of the violin has started playing again. As the violin's Banshee wail kept piercing her senses, she lurched forward with trembling and tired strides hoping for an end to this void somewhere. She can't afford to stop. She can't let this go on, she has to find a way out of this loop of her nightmare. The music keeps hammering her. And finally gasping for breath among her own strides Martha trips and falls to her face over the stone-covered floor with a thud. Question: What should I do if my life is going to end?
Answer: It shall all be over for me, you and everyone around us someday. The really funny part to this is that, we never really know when life, as such, is going to end for any of us. Sometimes the doctors fix us an approximate time, but still none of us really know the exact time we have to enrich ourselves with the air around us. Is this a race? Kind of, yes. This is a race with time, to which none of us really know when shall time exactly win and the finishing line shall be crossed. It has set the field, written the rules, and invited us to run along. Sometimes, it makes us run for our lives, at other times quite leisurely cracking a joke or two. How does it really feel to run a race, you know is destined to end? Like a marathon, it feels really great at first to run. But then, as age increases in some of us, this will to keep running gets lesser and lesser. The race may really end at any moment out of our sheer fate, yet still, some of us voluntarily choose to opt out very early. Question: What are a few bitter truths of life?
Answer: None really. Why shall a truth be bitter in the first place? People often compare a truth to a burning torchlight of justice. The next moment, I find them calling it a nessecary “evil”. And eventually, as we move through the alleys of our lives this same truth becomes bitter. The whole aroma of truth, mostly revolves around how it pricks into our souls. Sometimes, truths bring the warmest smiles and happiest tears to our eyes. Like a melody written in the pages of our heart, we embrace it with open arms, shower marigolds and daisies on it. And maybe that is how many promises of lifetime are made. For they are truths, truths of the moment, for sure. For truths that make the crystal clear waters of our heart unclear, we usually tend to be dissmissive of them. Those same truths, once showered of love, are now veiled into beautifully crafted lies. Why, have they lost their appeal? So you decorate your heart with lies, which you know will only make it worse. Then, arrives the day when truth becomes bitter. Like the stale food in the kitchen, which you have craved for before, but now it is unconsumable. You can neither enjoy its taste, nor throw it away. They say truth flows of bitterness, but so sweet it is; still, the pages written of truth is where lies beauty. It pains me— to see my face, distorted of the lies I made. They say truth brings hate and war, but it is adored on my doorstep; the smell of truth fills my heart. It pains me— to see your eyes, burning of rage, among my heart. One of the bitterest truths of life, is that, truth is never bitter itself. We often forget to embrace it. It rots among the decorated lies we gift our heart. And then one day, it is stale, bitter, unconsumable. Signing off, LOKI

Question: What are the things that you are grateful for?
Answer: The ability to tolerate negligence is much higher in men. It is as if infused in us from birth itself. We easily accept it. Somehow there is less expectation of getting something in return. Yes, not everyone is the same, but us, middle class boys, we trod negligence at every step in our lives. He can easily sacrifice everything that is left after spending a little on our monthly expenses. The rest of the money, he sends home with a big smile on his face, and an overflowing heart of love. Somewhere, the spectacles on his eyes has a scratched and half broken glass. Maybe, he should buy a new one. But he wont, for the thought itself is the end of the story. He writes a different story, the story of his old parents at home, the sister still in school who he wants to send for higher studies. His favourite shirt lies, not in the show glasses of big shops, but hanging among the roadside stalls. Not that his desires and dreams have died. His priorities lie elsewhere. The lack of luxury seems more homely than losing his self esteem. He walks home on foot. The boy of seventeen, running among the dim-lit streets of the locality has grown up today. Even after so much, he loses to life, everytime. Only to gamble again. I am grateful to be among such men, grateful to have such men to write about. Signing off, LOKI

Question: What is the purpose of the coil in an electrical motor?
Answer: The coil plays a vital yet often overlooked role in electrical motors. To understand its function, let me break down what's really happening inside. At its core, a motor is just an electromagnet in motion. When current flows through the coil wound around the motor's stationary stator, it creates a magnetic field. But on its own this field would just hang out, motionless. Here comes the rotor, the spinning part with its own coils. As coils on the rotor pass through the stationary magnetic field, they experience a force thanks to the electromagnetism. Magnetic poles are created that push and pull on the rotor coils based on the direction of current flow. This push and pull is what causes the rotor to begin rotating, like a merry-go-round slowly gaining momentum. Here comes the role of the coils, they play an important role in maintaining the rotation. You see, the current direction in both the stator and rotor coils is constantly switching to ensure the magnetic fields maintain the pull and push effect on each other. Without this alternating current, the process would grind to a halt. It is the coils conducting the current, and clever switching of current flow that enable both the alternating magnetic fields and precise control of rotor position needed for smooth, consistent spinning. Without coils carefully wrapped around both stationary and rotating parts, the motor would just sit there doing nothing. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: Can you tell me something inspiring?
Answer: The city of Kolkata was simmering with tension in the days leading up to August 1946. The Muslim League was becoming more vocal in their demand for Pakistan, clashing with rising Hindu nationalism. On 16th August, a procession celebrating the Muslim festival of Id-ul-Fitr was passing through the predominantly Hindu neighborhood of Ahiritola. Rumors spread that some Hindu celebrants had insulted their faith. Enraged, a mob of Muslim youth attacked the local Hindus. By evening, violence had engulfed the entire city. . . Armed mobs targeted Hindus, burning homes and businesses. The police seemed unable to control the mayhem and in some cases even joined in. Among those monitoring the situation with grave concern was Gopal Chandra Mukhopadhyay, a prominent Hindu lawyer and member of the Hindu Mahasabha party. While advocating non-violence, he believed the riots exposed that Hindus could no longer remain passive in the face of attack. The next two days saw the violence intensify, with over 4,000 casualties reported. With the police missing in action, entire streets had been taken over by rampaging gangs. People were barricaded inside their homes, fearing for their lives. Gopal realized Hindu residents needed to band together and defend themselves, or else face total annihilation. Inspired by courage under fire shown by revolutionaries like Khudiram Bose, he began quietly organizing neighborhood watch teams among Hindu locals. . . Armed with basic weapons like lathis and household tools, these groups patrol streets and bylanes that the police had abandoned. They escorted the injured to safety and guarded against further assaults. Morale rose seeing they weren't helpless in the face of violence. Though not initially intending to attack, the volunteers dispersed mobs threatening their neighborhoods with a show of strength and numbers. Word spread of this Hindu resistance, boosting spirit of communities under siege. . . The riots began dying down after 3 days of intense bloodshed. The death toll mounted over thousands. Amongst this, Gopal's community defense teams were praised for preventing further loss of lives in their areas, through strength and solidarity in difficult times. Gopal truly taught the Hindus of Kolkata how to stand up for themselves that day. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What are some of the best feelings in life?
Answer: Poeple say that negligence is born in the past, in old objects and people as time passes. What can I say, you know, when one becomes attached, responsibilities increase with the past. I can’t speak for everyone, but I understand that fulfilling the dreams of the past requires taking on responsibilities. The one who spoke of promises in the past should know they stand to fullfill them. What has touched their heart when those promises were made is not a matter of negligence. As time passes, the effort to fulfill the dreams of the past becomes more intense. Then, we try to be indifferent to the void of that past haunting us. Why make the promises then? Just since you can? Just since words dont cost you some rupees? Maybe yes, in the practical world around us, words dont have much value. But we sure listen to them, and see our future in them. One of the best feelings in life, is when a person gets old to you, and you still have that same excitement to be there for them as you had on the first day. Sometimes in life, our words do stick around, so why not everytime? Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What are some touching short poems on heartbreak?
Answer: FROZEN IN TIME There are some stories, which are best buried beauiful, in the soil of all laughter, and all the curtain falls. Where did those times go? When I was 16, and the chorus was yours? Are you lost? They say no, I say, never the same anymore. An “old decayed husk” or an Album of our memories, in which the deepest of secrets, shall be held. A ‘’fading twilight” or a boat on the end of earth, looking, where to begin? And, what if I am stubborn enough, To never let go? To cry my heart out, and never wipe my tears? I tell you darling, you look beautiful in there, frozen in time, between all our memories, laughters and tears, I tell you darling, you look beautiful in there. LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What is a brutal truth about life that needs to be said?
Answer: Each person is intricately connected to someone else's life in some way. Amidst all the sorrow, pain, disappointment, and failure, humans don't just live for themselves. Sometimes, people think about those who are entwined with their lives. When someone is not connected to anyone in life, they hastily make decisions without considering others. Even after enduring countless sorrows and hardships, when a person's mental state shatters, they think about those who are connected to their lives and make an effort to hold onto themselves. They embrace patience, like enduring sorrow and pain. Sometimes, people forget their own assured happiness because of those who are entwined with their lives. Before making any decision, a person thinks more about those who are connected to their lives. That is how many people in the world, tolerate infinite hardships and sorrow and still survive. Ever wondered how many people, even in their living state, give up all their joys and happiness? May you are one among them my friend. How many people acknowledge their fate and embrace both fortune and sorrow without judgement? And who keeps searching for it in vain? In this world, humans don't always live for themselves; some live thinking about others, enduring countless sorrows, struggles, and disappointments. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What made you think deep today?
Answer: After a storm, we get out of our homes to walk across the lawn. The lawn is never the same after the storm. Full of strewn old leaves, wet, giving of a a moist cool feeling in the air. We walk across, from the lawn to the road, without thinking much. The Sky is still thundering often. The smell of petrichor guiding our senses, we close our eyes as we move forward. It feels so cool and relieving dosen’t it? Same is with life. When a storm comes our way, it lashes at our windows, thunders in very high pitches. The wind blows like it is here to end everything today. And the Rain keeps pouring down, cooling the atmosphere down, like it always has done, for millions of years. And when the storm is over, it feels so serene, so relieving. The walk after the strom brings a bright smile to your face. Without the storm, there shall be no new beginning, and no relieving of our burdened past. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What are the most valuable things everyone should know?
Answer: Sometimes we misunderstand things out of the blue. Maybe the other person is wrong, or maybe they're not. Nevertheless, we still misunderstand. Words get tangled within words, one word suddenly envelops another. We lose the connection, the thread of our conversation. The clash of the present with the past continues. The future is always so far away. Yet, we still think the most about it. We keep carrying the burden of misunderstanding, carefully holding onto the tiny speck of misinterpretation in our hearts. Maybe the truth will never be known, but false pride and accusation will still linger. The river has always been there. Yet, people still choose to sit on the bank, refusing to traverse to the other side. There's one thing that I strongly feel. Maybe you're filled with pride, maybe anger has taken over for a few days. Still, take the time to stand in front of that person once. Perhaps they will say something, there might be something to say. Maybe what you're thinking is never the case. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What is the best life advice you would give?
Answer: A woman gets stuck in her child's love!!! For nine months and ten days, when one soul resides within another, forming a bond between two lives, that is where she gets stuck. Unable to walk, unable to speak, but the subtle emotions she feels from her baby inside her body. She gets stuck in those unexpressed tears. When the baby cries out loud, people wonder why she sheds tears like that for her child! Little do they know her mind is on an endless journey to know why her child is crying. Thousands of uncertainties get stuck in this way. Exhausted, her body breaks down repeatedly in broken sleep. She seems to be constantly restless in her child’s thoughts. When a fever arises in the deep of the night, she gets stuck in the turmoil of trying to bring down the temperature. Stuck in sleepless nights. Even after going to eat the food, when she feels, "Wait, has my baby eaten?". Sometimes, her food remains uneaten. Stuck in the magical aura of hearing the mother's call for the first time! It may sound a little strange to hear, but every woman experiences such a feeling at some point in her life!! Even if insulted a hundred thousand times, even being abused, she stays only for her child. The decision to go away repeatedly halts "mother". When the magical eyes of the mother turn towards the child. Where will I go, without my child... I won't be able to leave, it's not possible, she thinks!! A woman gets stuck in the love, affection, and magic of her child. I have a small advice in life for all those children when they grow up. Never forget your mother. My advice is very small, but it shall be of great blessing to me if all of you heed to it. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What are the truths that have made you stronger?
Answer: Some people always prefer to be alone. They eat alone, sleep alone, go out alone, and speak to themselves. They always find life in its solitary ideal, resting itself in a land where no attachments prevail. I dont know if it is something good or bad. But still, I learnt to respect these people. They are not bothered by diversity. They are like a deep abyss looking right back into your eyes. They tightly wrap their minds, keeping their mouths shut. Some people come and try to understand. They hear the words from within. But the voices never echo to the world outside. Hidden deep within, lies their deepest secrets, buried deep inside their souls. If they miss sleep at night, they don't find it in their eyes. The night flickers by them, like a everyday chore. For they have learnt long to be awake, to be kept awake by the same things they once closed their eyes in happiness for. You can spot them crying silently at midnight, cold, no one to hold a candle of warmth to their abandoned hearts. They continue to cry. Not loudly, but softly. No one hears. They are not heard. Their stories matter. Their tears have a place in my embrace. This is a truth that have made me stronger. Even those who we are not afraid of losing, one day they too will be lost, and perhaps our hearts shall be an endless abyss too. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What made you smile today?
Answer: I was having a very interesting thought within myself. What is happiness for the poor? One of my friends in college who came from a very poor household had a few words to say about this. I don't want love, I don't desire it, love doesn't fill my stomach! In our impoverished household, I witnessed from a young age the relationship of love between my parents. Whenever my father brought something a little fancy from the market, my mother wouldn't be happy. Instead she would spend the whole evening with a gloomy face. And my father would go about with caution as if he has done a very big mistake. In turn he would blame my mother for being thrifty when she saved money to buy cheap utensils. In their love, there was laughter and arguments, but the real joy reflected in their eyes when it was time to eat. That is when a huge smile appeared on my face. So food has become a symbol of love in the small poor household. Among all the twisted alleys of life, in everyday smile and tears, love has found its place. I realized, just like life, love too always finds a way in every household. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What are you thinking now?
Answer: Three lines from a Rabindra Sangeet, Era Sukher Lagi Chahe Prem, Prem mele-na, Sukh chole jaay The lines mean, People want happiness in love, but they never find love, happiness goes away in chasing it. Who sees the fatigue and insomnia in our eyes? I have heard people understand each other. But then why does the person of our heart dosen’t understand us? Why do we fail to understand ourselves at times? Doesn't a person know how to love? They want love. The chest that craves love, the heart that cries out for love, why doesn't anyone love it? People throw love away so easily! They always pour their heart to a mirror which never reflects. Where does a person find solace? How many times, in the pursuit of simple happiness, does a person suffer in various pains, and who keeps track of that? Every day, people endure the agony of their hearts! Such fatigue, frustration of not achieving, and endless complaints. Those who seek love are deceived! Those who find love are the ones who deceive. Such Irony! People search for happiness in love, yet love itself takes away their happiness, it doesn't allow people to be happy! Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: Can you write something so deep that it would make me feel something?
Answer: Do our mothers feel jealous too? During childhood, we show jealousy towards our mothers when siblings receive slightly more attention. But do our mothers get jealous too at any point? Think for a girl. When another new mother is created after marriage, and her child grows up and lives with separate people. She divides the love for her "mother" and provides so much care to another new mother. Does that not make our own mother jealous? The girl who used to show anger to her own mother at will now tries to reconcile with another new mother. The mother who took care of her when she was sick, she spends only but a few days with her in her illness, and yet, looks after that the tea of another mother is served at the right time. Does that make her “mother” jealous? Think for a boy. The boy who always used to be at her every footstep, now that same boy tries to melt the anger of his wife. The same boy who used to take her whereabouts all the day, now is tensed about the whereabouts of his own children. Does that not make his “mother” jealous? Mom, are you not jealous? I am sure there is jealousy or possesiveness towards mothers’ love. But I have realized that being a mother means selfless, unconditional love, which binds us together. I am not crying, you are. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What is one quality you admire in people?
Answer: "Mother" is a small word. But within it, it encompasses the vastness of a mountain-like love and affection. The depth of this small word cannot be expressed even if we combine all the words in the world. However, there are only few among us who can understand this love. As we grow older, amidst laughter and conversations with our friends and loved ones, sometimes we unintentionally forget about this person named "Mother". Sometimes, we feel embarrassed to present our mother in front of our friends, holding onto our own status. Perhaps, she may not be able to speak in a smart language, hidden behind a veil, and we foolishly think this will diminish our respect infront of our friends. We often abuse people over their mother. We verbally abuse the birth of a person and how their mother gave them birth without even thinking of our own mother We degorate women and pass comments just to be “dank” among friends without even thinking how our mothers will shudder at such conduct of ours. We often forget that it is this very mother who taught us our first word. She is the one who taught us to walk, provided us with primary education, taught us to overcome hardships by leaning on her shoulder. She is the one who fed us when we were hungry, and took care of us when we were sick. It also happens that we feel the absence of this person named "Mother" only when it is too late. What is one quality I admire in people? Their respect for their mother in all spheres of their life. Not only infront of their own mothers, but how they show respect to them in every small action of their life. Be it in a public place, or on the internet. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What makes you jealous?
Answer: The favourite person who was our all weather friend. The gang with whom having tea at the locality stall were the best moments of the day. The playlist of all those favourite songs from years and years ago. The chats and conversations which were the sweetest of all. All those planned trips which kept getting cancelled. And all the random meetups which were never planned. All those promises and oaths of forever given with a smile of happiness. Where did we lose them? Why did we let them slip, let them exhaust? Why were we not able to hold to them when it mattered the most. What makes me jealous? The people who are living and holding on to these little gems. Maybe they got lost in some forgotten alley of life, but ones who are living them and holding on to them are very fortunate indeed. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: Do any authors hate writing?
Answer: Anyone who writes stuff out that is their own content, can be comfortably called an author. Us, authors are perhaps some of the most interesting people you will encounter. To begin with this question, no one really authors content without love or interest for their subject. But then at times, writing those thoughts out can become a thing we pull away from. It gets to a point where authors may hate writing out just since their thoughts ain’t satisfactory. Satisfaction of one’s thoughts on paper matters a lot. An unsatisfied peice of writing feels like an unfinished part of myself, that should be burned in the pyre of memories. At points, when none of your our thoughts seem satisfactory, the whole process of writing something to just fill in the gap becomes a dreaded lump in one corner of our heart. Now, there is another rare occurence. Authors hating their own masterpeices. This is rare, very rare, but it happens nonetheless. You create a peice of absolute beauty that you want burned right the next moment. Why so? I dont know. Our emotions sometimes dont have any specific meaning, rather its just the way we feel. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: Are we really independent?
Answer: WHERE SHALL THE FLAG FLY? The debt of the soul, a song full of dream, In this hope, yes, in that hope, Even if we forget a few words, Opened hearts with laughter amidst the chaos, Memories leave as they go, Leaving behind all the promises. The restlessness of youth, Where is the commotion today? What use is your heart drowning now of? Tears that have flowed, Lost in the flow of time. Tell me, why don't you speak your heart out? Has the flag of independence not flown? How many deaths, how many dark stains, On which land will this flag rise? Today, I have been thinking. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What doesn't make sense to you?
Answer: Seema went to her school reunion after a gap of nearly 20 years. She felt a little akward inside, being a housewife. She also has started a small buissness of jewellery and cosmetics recently. She remembered her friends being very supportive of her in past. As she walked past them, she overheard them conversing how no proffesion is small and every proffesion has its own value. Encouraged, she shares her story with them. But to her utter surprise, as soon as they hear it, they begin behaving strangely with her. They avoid and alienate as if she is below their “standards”. What dosen’t make sense to me? The morals people preach, and then refuse to abide themselves. As in this case, they failed to think about her efforts to earn something for herself and went ahead judging her and placing in standards that don’t even have any real meaning. They did not have the thoughts to think how she could have been married off very early by her parents. And how, she might be making the best efforts possible to earn for herself, after taking care of her family. Its time to change, not just preach, but change for real. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What is on your mind at the moment?
Answer: The forms of Silence. People have told me how silence never feels good to them. It feels like an unpleasant termination. But to someone like me, who has mastered the art of silence, it has a lot of different meanings. Sometimes, silence is the only form of communication, you look, you let the other person speak. It is beautiful that way. Sometimes, silence is like a dive into the world of understanding, to evaluate where do we really stand at the moment, and it is really important to do so. Sometimes, silence is restraining yourself from blurting out statements which may have very unpleasant impact in the near future. Sometimes, silence is a way of taking care of yourself in solitude while caring less about the world around you. Sometimes, silence is carefully planning your road ahead, but also bidding a road goodbye. Silence is a termination for sure, but not always an unpleasant one. This is what is on my mind at the moment. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: Why should we not chase perfection?
Answer: Those who dislike you, no matter how hard you try, will never have a place in their hearts for you! Even if you excel in your good deeds, they will find faults in them. It seems that people tend to consider the mistakes of those they like as correct, while considering the correct actions of those they dislike as mistakes. Day after day, you continue to become the reason for their dislike, they will never have a single positive thought towards you. They will only think about how they can make you suffer more. No person in the world can be loved by everyone, and in the end, someone will always be disliked by someone else. But that doesn't mean that life stops for you. Even if disliked by everyone in the world, if there is just one person who can understand you correctly, love you, and one who likes you, then the disapproval of everyone else will not cause you pain. You will only find pain when you see someone whom you love or those who love you, it is them only who dislike you! Why make futile efforts just to gain the hatred of those who receive your love in return? The one who will like you, will do so without any reason or condition. Believe that there are people in the world who love you and like you and that is the reason you are alive. And that is why, never chase perfection. Be yourself. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What is an unpopular opinion you hold?
Answer: I have noticed that even people who believe in "Age Doesn't Matter" can change when it comes to relationships. Initially, no matter how much they say that age doesn't matter in love, at some point, the age difference does become a reason for the relationship to deteriorate! There is a significant difference between an adult and a mature person. Once a person turns 18, they are considered an adult, but there is no specific age for maturity, whether it's 18, 40, or any other number. Now, when a mature person is involved with a teenager or someone younger, they don't necessarily find the same behavior or mindset in the other person. And it's not unnatural to not find that compatibility. While age may not be a problem at the beginning of a relationship, in certain aspects of life, the age difference becomes the main concern. Each person's needs also change with age, and it's natural for their desires to not align with each other. What a 28-year-old woman desires will not be the same as what a 35 or 40-year-old woman desires. The same difference is applicable to the desires of a 28-year-old man and a 35 or 40-year-old man. If you want to maintain a relationship that is emotionally fulfilling and stable, it is crucial to have compatibility in each other's needs. In this case, it is advisable to choose someone who is close to your own age and fulfills the desires that you have at your age. If a decision is made based on the belief that "age doesn't matter" without considering the emotional impact, it can lead to lifelong regrets! But then, many exceptions exist too! Infact so many that they cannot be called exceptions anymore! Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What was your most interesting thought today?
Answer: You satisfied yourself with an illusion, leaving me to think about it every day! You lie on a bed of affection every night, delighting your body, while I spend those nights in solitude. The death of a person's love can still be accepted, but can one easily accept living while surrendering oneself to someone else's touch? No, it's not possible! Every night, you dream of finding happiness little by little, while I search for the courage to survive, to find strength. In the futile attempt of wanting to be a little happy, I repeatedly dive into the abyss of forgetting. You continue to seek happiness in affection, and I delve deeper into the depths of emptiness, reminiscing about you. What you consider love and happiness, I consider it a venomous memory that haunts me little by little. These are the most interesting thoughts I had today. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What made you angry today?
Answer: No job is insignificant. Yet we strive to build ourselves for our dream profession little by little since childhood. Amongst many, one coveted profession of dreams is one of a teacher. People sculpt themselves slowly, with the support of their parents, giving their all to fulfill their child's dreams. But when the places of dream fulfillment become filled with corruption, the deserving are hindered, degrees are lost to monetary influence, then their blood, sweat, and the weight of the degree turn into a nightmare. After that, they are forced to abandon their dreams and engage in some other work. Lack of employment leads to a generation averse to education. The futile effort, wasted blood, the mountain of degrees unused, and the shattered dreams of an entire generation are not taken into account by anyone. Many talented and hardworking young boys and girls get lost in the darkness. And those who cannot bear the torment end up taking their own lives. Nobody gets to know that those are not deaths, but killings of dreams, one dream at a time. What made me angry today? The fact that this process has become a vicious cycle in society. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What made you upset today?
Answer: "I am not feeling well, mother." These words echo in our hearts today, those are the words Swapnadeep spoke on the phone. Swapnadeep, a first-year. Bengali Honours student at Jadavpur University. He along with the secret of his death has died, having fallen from the rooftop. Fingers point towards Ragging. Alright, where exactly will the responsibility for "Ragging" lie? This is not just a two-line introduction, but it has turned into a disease. We need a solution to this problem. Today, my friend, I haven't come to write the right answer. I've come to shed some tears, to reflect a little. We, the students, where are we heading? As a distant observer, it seems that studying in a good university in the city will lead to a successful life and career. And what welcome gift are we offering him? Ragging? Mental and physical abuse? In reality, they are not students, but wild animals dressed in the attire of students. Let it stop, let it stop, Oh God! Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What are some things most people take for granted?
Answer: I was walking back home today. A cloudy rumbling sky. It has been like this for the past few days. Everyday, the sky would ask me, “Shall I rain, and we two shall embrace ourselves?” And I would frown, and give a stern look, “No! not now please, I dont want to get wet, let me reach home” And, with a sad face, it would keep rumbling on, until I had reached home. Thereafter, it would pour on, relentlessly. The selfish me, who didnt care for it’s wishes, would enjoy its downpour from the comfort of my Balcony. And then today, again, it had been rumbling. But Karma as it is, the Sky was in no mood to listen to my pleas. One drop, two drop, a drizzle, and then it poured. Poor me! I wasn’t even carrying the umbrella. I made a run for my house, still there was no respite from its embrace. It had always wanted me, and it had me for itself today. It was me who took it’s timing and wishes for granted. Look at me now. Having quite a cough! Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: Is fear a good or bad thing?
Answer: A lover’s Ramble: Why do you get angry suddenly like this? Tell me, even my beautiful tea feels bitter having seen your gloomy face. The colorful and lively face of mine becomes gloomy. In the scorching heat of your fire stare, both my body and mind are burnt! In your anger, a strange fear is created in my heart! At night, I lose sleep, and insomnia engulfs me! Even the sweet morning feels strange. I keep trying to focus on work but keep getting distracted! In your anger and contempt, even the walls of my heart transform into pale houses of cards, and the gentle breeze around me starts to flow cautiously! Why does your silence in contempt appear so terrifying? Tell me, yet, why do I gaze at your angered face with awe, even though I am scared? Your huffed face, oh how I adore it. Your anger brings dense dark clouds into my world, and I see emptiness in every direction! I look towards your huffed and puffed face and indulge in love, yet I am startled by the terrifying form of your anger again and again! I dont know if this fear is good or bad, but it is a part of love alright! The answers to the question gives you a lot of perspectives of fear, I gave one from my side! Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What are some of the best things I can do to improve people's lives?
Answer: We people sit and overthink on the anxities of our life. We keep overthinking, and as time passes, the thread of our thoughts gets lengthier and further away. At some point, that thread becomes too long for us to pull it back. Then, we that same thread we try to sew the insecurities, anxities and wounds of our heart and soul. But, who is good at sewing themselves? No one. The wounds and insecurities, never really fully heal, and our griefs are all but supressed before peeping out again later. All we need is a true friend, who can sew those insecurities and wounds of our heart, and finally help us heal. What is the best thing you can do to help people improve their lives? Just be that friend to them. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What made you happy recently?
Answer: Back in my childhood, I had a great affection for pencil boxes. Whenever I visited shopping malls, fairs or stationary stores, I used to cry and be clingy to buy the pencil boxes. I kept them well-maintained and always kept the pens and pencils inside organized. To be honest, I never used to recieve a lot of tem. That's why I kept them in excellent condition, so that they keep their flair for long. I used to think, when I grow up and have enough money, I will make a collection of many pencil boxes. Today, having grown up, the small desires of my childhood have faded away with time. Once, I was teary-eyed, and thought I would buy a lot of pencil boxes. When I remembered that today, I smiled to myself. It felt nostalgic and happy at the same time. Life is amusing. The small desires we have, change with the flow of time, but the boat of life still sails on. Singing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What are your realizations when you get older?
Answer: A few days ago, I had a fascinating experience. I had always thought that humans, most of the time, do not prioritize speaking first. But why is that? When I was young, I used to think that there wasn't much to say, hence the difficulty in finding words. But slowly, I realized a change within myself. It seemed to me that there wasn't just one reason why people don't speak up. Perhaps, or maybe, something has diluted within the vast ocean of words. Lost within the waves, unable to understand what to say. Perhaps, or maybe, the ink on the pages of words has faded, leaving behind empty spaces. Maybe the ink of love and intimacy, is not enough to write the fairytale anymore. Who knows, maybe they want the other person to speak first. Maybe they want to understand the opposite person through their expressions. Sometimes, in life, you have to paint your face. Perhaps, they want to paint her own face to the words of others before responding. Signing off, LOKI

Name: Lokenath Roy
Question: What's one interesting thing you'd want to share to the world?
Answer: On the day, August 1st, 1971, the United States was observing a weekly holiday. However, unlike the typical American administration, which took the side of the Pakistani military's genocide and oppression, a significant portion of the general public stood in solidarity against the ongoing atrocities and persecution by the Pakistani armed forces in Bangladesh. Exactly forty-eight years ago, the world witnessed the first-ever charity concert, "The Concert For Bangladesh," held at Madison Square Garden in New York. It created history in the world of music, serving as a memorable event for the cause of Bangladesh's independence, protesting against the genocide and helping in providing aid to refugees. The war-ravaged nation of Bangladesh(East Pakistan at that time), with its struggling population and lack of resources, became known to the global community through various media outlets, including the BBC. At that time, residing in the United States, Pandit Rabindra Shankar Chowdhury (Ravi Shankar), felt the plight of those displaced and affected by the inhumane circumstances. It was this desire to stand by the side of the Bengalis in such a deplorable situation that led to the idea of the concert in Pandit Ravi Shankar's mind. Following the breakup of The Beatles, this concert marked Harrison's first direct involvement in a live performance. Eric Clapton also contributed to the concert, performing nearly five months after his last performance at the time. Bob Dylan, after a long halt since 1969, made a comeback to the stage in front of an audience. August 1st, 1971, witnessed a remarkable concert at Madison Square Garden in New York, which became a significant historical event. It featured maestros like Ravi Shankar, the sitar virtuoso Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, and tabla maestro Alla Rakha Khan performing for the cause of Bangladesh. They were followed by George Harrison and Ringo Starr of The Beatles, who each performed separately, along with additional performances by Leon Russell, Billy Preston, and renowned singer-songwriter Bob Dylan. Guitarist Eric Clapton also graced the concert with his guitar skills. The concert concluded with George Harrison's iconic song, "Bangladesh." Not many people in India know about this exceptional concert. It deserves a mention in this answer. Signing off, LOKI

Question: Who is a successful person?
Answer: Once I was sitting in my room, thinking how everyone seems to have different, and at times, a multi faceted definition of success for themselves. To someone, the big cabin in the sixth floor of the Posh Corporate building is some serious success. To someone else, to be able to make a buissness is what he or she writes below success in their book of life. Success to someone, can be getting many books published in their name to as trivial is having a content, happy family under a roof. It all seemed to have infinite dimensions, until I noticed a pattern in them all. Everyone wants to achieve something, they want to win the challenge they have set for themselves, whatever the challenge may be. But in these challenges, something much more valuable is lost. People are unable to grasp themselves. Even before they can grasp, society, family, responsibilities, duties, the country, friends and relatives divide their bounty among themselves. And the day they finally find themselves, in a forgotten alley of life; that day they cannot fly anymore. Life, is not a prize to be won. It is something you need to live every moment of. To find yourself. Just like time, once gone, it does not return. All efforts for success is in the name of a better life, yet by the time we proceed to truly live that way, our souls are eroded of life’s passing. Who is a successful person? There is still no definite answer. But to lose oneself in its pursuit, surely cannot be success in its true form. Signing off, LOKI

Why not enjoy some of them toghther on occasional tours like this?” I noticed a shy smile form across the face of Mrs. Chaterjee. What made me happy today? Question: What is something that you will never do?
Answer: Once I heard of a funny, yet very deeply reflecting conversation, regarding an arranged marraige. The Parents of the groom has gone to the see the bride at her home. The face of the girl glows in happiness. The boy's father: "If adorned with all adornments, she will become an incomparable reflection of Mata Lakshmi herself." The girl suddenly is dampened, as if someone put dark clouds over the ray of light that was adoring her face. The boy's mother: "Yes, a fortunate match." The boy's father: "With the mark of a lotus imprinted on these feet adorned with anklets, a new home will prosper. But the price of the home... thirty-four lakhs!" The girl remains silent. Her head hanging down, as her conscience hammers into the abyss. The boy's mother: "My son is learning driving these days. Question: What is freedom?
Answer: My idea of what does freedom truly mean came from a story by Rabindranath Tagore, which I read in childhood. In the story, he writes: One day at school, the teacher asked in class “What is freedom?” Everyone seemed a bit perplexed to find a generalised answer to the question, until one boy rose up and said, “Sir, freedom is the right we are granted to do anything we wish to”. The answer did not please the teacher, he countered him, “So what if we murder someone, or rob someone’s house from our wish, does these things come under freedom too?” He dissmissed the class without providing any concrete answer to the question, and rather leaving it to the students to realize for themselves. Interestingly, that guy found himself at home alone that day with his younger brother, who was a adopted child. His mother had gone to the place of of his aunt, and left them both, two mangoes to eat. While giving the mango to his brother, he took the smaller one, while he gave his brother the larger mango. This made both him and his brother very happy. Immidiately, it struck him. He ran to the house of his teacher and said; “Sir, I have come to understand the meaning of freedom. Freedom is the right to do something that makes me truly happy, while at the same time not harming anyone else in the process” So, I always followed this in life when it came to defining freedom for myself. Freedom is the right to take any view or action that makes me happy while at the same time causes no harm to anyone else in society. Signing off, LOKI

Question: What is something you wish people knew?
Answer: Sir Ratna Tata, an Indian Billionaire, was fined 50 euros for the crime of food waste at a restaurant in Germany. This small amount of money was not a big issue for him. However, what he learned that day from the restaurant was truly invaluable to him. He wrote, "Germany is one of the most industrially advanced countries in the world. Once, I went to a restaurant in Hamburg with my colleague. Since we were very hungry, my colleague ordered quite a bit of food. Unfortunately at the end of the meal, we saw that we had about one-third of the food still left" Later, when my colleague and I were about to leave the restaurant, an elderly woman who seemed to be a staff there looked annoyed. She said, "You should not waste your food." My colleague replied to the woman, "We paid for the food. How does it matter if some of it gets left out? What's your problem?" This response made the woman quite upset. She immediately made a phone call to someone. Soon, a person dressed in the clothing of a social security organization arrived. After listening to everything, the person fined my colleague and me 50 euros each. I was shocked by the incident. Then the official said in an very steady tone, "You can only order what you can eat." "Money is yours, but resources belong to society" Sir Ratan Tata learned a very valuable lesson that day. That even if we have the money to spend, we should not spend it in a way that it leads to wastage of resources, as they belong to all of us, and all we do is take from the collective pool. In the times of Energy Crisis, Global Warming, poverty and food crisis, this lesson is something I really wish all of us knew and applied in our lives. Signing off, LOKI

Question: What is a successful life for you? Why?
Answer: Let me tell you a story. One day, at the end of classes, when I was leaving university, my shoe strap tore as I was moving towards the bus stand. I limped forward with some difficulty and saw an elderly person repairing shoes, in front of a group of three or four school-going boys. I was able to discern them belonging to a prestigious school nearby from their uniform. I stood a little away from the gathering of the boys. A little later, one of the boy's shoes was done sewing by the old man. The boy immidiately threw a ten rupee note towards him in a manner of ignorance. The note even slipped mid air as the old man grasped for it with his hands. If he hadn't held it, the money would have flown away. The boys, who could have been no less concerened, left the place giggling among themselves. I felt bad and walked ahead. I asked, "Grandpa, can you fix my Kito?" The old man gave a smile and nodded his head. I handed him over my sandal. Then when my Kito was mended, I knelt down and touched the feet of the elderly person with my hand. He stood up with great surprise and looked at me in amazement, his bewildered eyes asking me the question “why?” I said, "You are like my grandfather. You gave me your hand to help me with my Kito which I wear on my feet, so I showed respect to you by touching your feet." I turned around and walked towards my bus. It got a little emotional for me, as I thought, how everyone deserves respect in our society, irrespective of who they are, or what proffesion they follow. To give such equal respect to everyone, is what I think means to be a successful person in life. This success cannot be measured by the bank balance or the social status one has, but only by the love people reciprocate towards us. Signing off, LOKI

Question: What is something you want to say to everyone?

Question: How cool is your mother?

My mother and I keep arguing like this, but then I think how only that person who is always by my side when I am sick, with a fever, and lying in bed for hours. That person who stays up late to give me water is the only person who will always say the same thing to me every day. —"Have you drunk water after eating?" I forget to ask you, but you never forget, even for a day. And just since you never forget, I am relieved because I know that in this world, at least one person is always there for me, who will never leave me alone, no matter how far away they are. Answer: I have a friend at my university. Lets call her “Atri”. Atri is a calm girl, soft spoken yet has a very sharp mind. She likes to stand up for herself, which I something I really admire. At the same time, she tries to stay as far away as possible from all types of fights and university politics. This is something she always wanted to get off her chest to the larger audience. I went inside straight away, and called “Bhaiya, hear once! -Yes, tell me atri -Bhaiya I wont go to university in public bus from tommorow -Why Atri? -Some guys try to touch me innapropriately, and also pass rude comments on my body. Immidiately, I saw the colour of the face of bhaiya go pale. He seemed at a loss of words. Before he could say anything I left the room with steady footsteps as the door banged behind me.” Did Bhaiya change? Maybe. Question: What are some of the most weird human behavior?
Answer: Some of the weirdest human behaviors stem from our desire for social approval and status. We do all sorts of strange things just to fit in or appear "cool" to others. Keeping up with others in an invisible race: We obsess over what others have - their houses, cars, clothes, and any symbols of wealth or status. We constantly compare ourselves and feel inadequate, driving us to acquire more things we often don't really need. Conspicuous consumption: We buy luxuries and designer goods not because we actually value them, but to display our wealth and taste to others. The logos and brands become more important than the functions of the products themselves. We consume conspicuously to gain the approval of strangers. Following the herd: When a new trend takes off, many people jump on the bandwagon without critically evaluating if the trend even makes sense. From popular diets to exercise crazes, we blindly follow what "everyone" seems to be doing to avoid feeling left out. Pretending to like things: We often pretend to enjoy certain foods, activities or interests, solely to appear more cultured, sophisticated or appealing to others. We feign interest in things we don't actually value, just to fit some idealized image. Signing off, LOKI

Question: What is the difference between thinking and thought?
Answer: Thinking is the active process of mind, while thought is the product, the result or outcome of thinking. One is a verb, the other a noun. Thinking involves reasoning, pondering, reflecting and considering possibilities. It is an internal conversation, a wrestling with ideas. Like music played on invisible strings, thinking has its own rhythm, melody and harmony. A thought, on the other hand, is a single note struck from that thinking, a crystallization of meaning. A thought may linger or float away, spawn new thoughts or drift into oblivion. Yet thoughts do not fully capture the multidimensional act of thinking. They are but snapshots of a process that continues ceaselessly, beyond our perception and control. Thoughts come and go; thinking continues. So thinking might be called the flowing river, thoughts the bubbles rising to its surface. The river runs deep and strong regardless, though each bubble shimmers with its own vigour before popping into silence. Signing off, LOKI

Question: What is the highest temperature ever recorded in the universe?
Answer: The core of the Sun currently has a temperature of around 15 million degrees Celsius. But that pales in comparison to temperatures observed elsewhere in the universe. When stars explode as supernovas, they release massive amounts of energy and heat up to unbelievable temperatures. The core of supernova explosions can reach temperatures of 100 billion degrees Celsiust! To put that into perspective: The temperature at the core of the Sun is hot enough to melt nearly any kind of rock, yet the supernova temperature is over 6,000 times hotter. The hottest man-made temperature ever achieved on Earth is around 100 million degrees Celsius in nuclear fusion reactors. A supernova core is 1,000 times hotter than that. The energy released would be catastrophic. So what allows these objects to reach such extremes? It all comes down to gravity and density. When a star is forming or a supernova is exploding, the material is crushed inward by the immense gravity. Question: What is the difference between Data Analytics, Data Analysis, Data Mining, Data Science, Machine Learning, and Big Data?
Answer: Data Analytics: This refers to the process of inspecting, transforming and modeling data to discover useful information, suggest conclusions and support decision making. Analytics uses techniques from statistics, machine learning, and visualization. It is a broad field that encompasses multiple types of analysis. Data Analysis: This refers to examining raw data to obtain useful information and derive conclusions. It involves using analytical tools and techniques to organize and interrogate data with the goal of summarizing it into useful insights. Data analysis is a subset of data analytics focused more on deriving insights from historical data. Data Mining: This involves searching large amounts of data for patterns and relationships that can be considered useful. It uses statistical, machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to discover patterns in large datasets that can help predict future behavior and trends. Data mining can be seen as a more advanced form of data analysis focused on automated discovery of insights. Data Science: This encompasses the broad set of skills, techniques and approaches needed to extract insights from data. It includes data analytics, machine learning, statistical modeling and data visualization. Data scientists combine expertise in mathematics, programming and domain knowledge to analyze complex datasets and build data-driven solutions. Machine Learning: This is a subset of artificial intelligence that uses statistical techniques to give computers the ability to "learn" from data without being explicitly programmed. Machine learning algorithms "learn" by analyzing training data to identify patterns, make predictions or perform tasks. When given new data, they can apply what they've "learned" to yield useful results. Big Data: This refers to the enormous volumes of data that businesses now have available due to the digital world we live in. Big data has three main characteristics: volume, velocity and variety. Industry analysts say any dataset exceeding terabytes or petabytes in size qualifies as "big data." Big data technologies and techniques enable the extraction of value from these massive datasets. Question: What is the physical significance of wave function?
Answer: I feel the wave function is one of the most interesting yet puzzling concepts in quantum mechanics. It provides a description of quantum systems like atoms and subatomic particles in terms of waves and probabilities. But what about its physical significance To help you understand this, let me start with a simple classical analogy. Imagine throwing a pebble into a pond. The pebble disturbs the water, creating circular wave patterns that propagate outward. These water waves carry information about the initial disturbance i.e the mass, velocity and position of the pebble. Now imagine things in the quantum scale. You must have heard subatomic particles like electrons also behave like waves in addition to behaving like particles, this is called dual nature. So we represent quantum particles using wave functions just like we represent water waves using mathematical functions of motion. But here's where things get weird. The wave function does not directly represent an electron, it represents all the possible states an electron could be in and the likelihood of finding the electron in each state. So the wave function essentially contains all the possible information we can know about a particle in a probabilistic way. When we measure the position of an electron, its wave function instantly "Vanishes" and we observe it in a definite location. Prior to measurement, the wave function describes a smeared out probability distribution, showing the electron could be anywhere within a certain region. So in a sense, the wave function represents the mystries of the quantum world. It encodes the probabilities of observing different possible outcomes from measurements. The physical significance is that it allows us to make statistical predictions about the behavior of atomic and subatomic systems, even though we cannot predict the exact position, momentum or energy of a single particle. To summarize, the wave function physically represents a combination of possibilities - a superposition of states, that collapses into classical definiteness only upon measurement. It is perhaps the weirdest and most fascinating concept in all of physics! Signing off, LOKI

Question: What is the difference between GDP and GNP?
Answer: GDP and GNP are two key measurements of a country's economic output. Understanding the difference between the two can help clarify how a country’s economy is evaluated. Gross domestic product, or GDP, refers to the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders during a specific time period. It aims to measure everything produced domestically. Gross national product, or GNP, is slightly different. GNP includes GDP but also adds the net income a country's citizens and businesses earn abroad. So in simple terms: GDP = Value of goods and services produced within a country's borders GNP = GDP + Net income earned abroad Let me break this down further: GDP focuses only on production within a country's physical borders. It looks at output created by domestic residents and organizations, regardless of where the income is actually earned. For example, if a US company makes $100 million by selling products to customers in India, that $100 million would be included in the US GDP. This is because the production happened within the US, even though the income was earned here in India. In contrast, GNP factors in income earned abroad by residents of that country. So in the example I gave above, GNP would include that same $100 million in output but would then subtract any production costs and foreign taxes paid. The net income earned abroad is added to GDP to calculate GNP. Therefore, GNP reflects the total income of a country's citizens from all sources, both domestic and foreign. It provides a more accurate and realistic picture of the resources available for domestic consumption. Signing off, LOKI

Question: Who first gave the idea of introducing the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in India?
Answer: The idea of introducing a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in India that applies equally to all citizens regardless of religion, gender or ethnicity has been proposed and debated for decades. There are strong arguments both for and against implementing a UCC. I will try to provide an in-depth yet readable discussion on this complex issue: The idea of a UCC is enshrined in Article 44 of the Indian Constitution under Directive Principles of State Policy. It states, "The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India." Thus, the Indian Constitution envisioned a common set of laws for all citizens instead of separate personal laws based on religion. However, Article 44 is a Directive Principle, meaning it serves as a guiding force rather than an enforceable provision. Debate around UCC gained momentum in the 1980s during the Shah Bano case. Shah Bano, a Muslim divorcee, claimed alimony under the Indian legal code which is gender-neutral. However, the Muslim Personal Law Board argued that Muslim divorce and alimony matters should be governed by Sharia law and not 'civil' laws. Supporters of a UCC argue that it will help achieve gender justice and equality by setting the same standards for marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption, maintenance, and succession for all citizens. They say a UCC can help protect minority women's rights and address issues like triple talaq and polygamy that discriminate against women. A UCC will also strengthen national unity and integrity by overriding divisive identity politics based on religion. However, opponents argue that religion-based personal laws reflect the cultural ethos of minority communities. They see a UCC as an assault on religious freedom and identity. There are also complexities in reaching a consensus on what should be included in a UCC given India's diversity. While the idea of a UCC sounds progressive in principle, the sheer complexity of implementing it makes it a politically controversial issue. Any attempt by the state to enforce a UCC may face resistance from minority groups who see personal laws as vital to protect their religious identity. Signing off, LOKI

Question: What is adiabatic index? Why is its value always greater than unity?
Answer: The adiabatic index, also known as the ratio of specific heats, is a measure of how much a gas will compress under pressure. It tells us how the pressure and volume of a gas are related when changes occur so quickly that no heat is exchanged with the surroundings. So in simple terms, the adiabatic index tells us how "springy" a gas is. Gases with a high adiabatic index are less compressible and spring back strongly when released, like a taut rubber band. Gases with a lower adiabatic index are more compressible and spring back more gently, like a softer rubber band. The adiabatic index depends on two things, like, how many degrees of freedom the gas particles have, and how much those degrees of freedom are used for storing energy versus transferring energy between particles. For a monatomic gas like helium, the particles only have translational degrees of freedom. So when you compress the gas, the particles just end up moving faster. This leads to a high adiabatic index close to 1.67. or diatomic gases like nitrogen and oxygen, the particles have both translational and rotational degrees of freedom. So when you compress the gas, the particles can either move faster or rotate faster. This uses up some of the energy, leading to a lower adiabatic index around 1.4. For polyatomic gases like carbon dioxide, the particles have translational, rotational and vibrational degrees of freedom. So there are even more ways for the gas to absorb the compression energy, leading to a much lower adiabatic index around 1.3. So in short, the more "wiggle room" gas particles have to absorb compression energy, the lower the adiabatic index will be. Now let me get to the fun and intuitive part- why is the adiabatic index always greater than 1? This simply comes down to the fact that gases, by nature, resist compression. If the adiabatic index was 1 or less, that would mean the gas volume would either stay the same or increase when subjected to more pressure! But we know from everyday experience that gases tend to occupy less space when compressed, so their adiabatic index must always be greater than 1. Signing off, LOKI

Answer: Let's start with the basics. A flame is the visible part of fire resulting from a chemical reaction called combustion. For combustion to occur you need three things - fuel, oxygen and heat. When you light a match or lighter, the resulting flame starts where the fuel meets oxygen, usually at the tip. So why is the tip hottest? It all comes down to oxygen availability and how fast the combustion reaction occurs. At the tip, oxygen has the easiest access to the fuel. This allows the fuel and oxygen to react most rapidly, generating the most heat. Think of it like a race, the faster something happens, the more energy is released. The bluish-white color of the tip also tells us it's the hottest part. Higher flame temperatures produce light with shorter wavelengths, shifting from orange to yellow to white and finally blue. Further down the flame, oxygen has to diffuse through layers of slower burning fuel to reach unburned fuel particles. This slower reaction results in lower flame temperatures, represented by the orange and yellow colors. Signing off, LOKI

Question: Do I really need to put my phone on airplane mode while flying?
Answer: Yes you should definitely put your phone in airplane mode during the entire flight for various good reasons. Let's understand this from the ground up. When a plane takes off and is flying high in the sky, your phone is still trying its best to stay connected to cell phone towers on the ground. But here's the problem - the plane is flying so high that your phone's signal is now extremely weak and unstable. Imagine your phone screaming at the top of its tiny lungs, "Hey cell tower! Can you hear me?! I'm up here! Helloooooo!". But the cell tower is just a tiny little dot on the ground, deaf to your phone's cries. Your phone will now start boosting its transmission power to the max, desperately trying to connect to a tower. But all this effort is just wasting your phone's battery life and potentially interfering with the plane's sensitive electronic equipment. Putting your phone in airplane mode simply cuts off this futile struggle by turning off the transmission of radio signals. Your phone can now sleep peacefully for the duration of the flight instead of wasting energy. The plane's sensitive navigation equipment is also not disturbed. Electronics on a plane are highly sensitive because they rely on receiving very weak radio signals to calculate the plane's exact position, altitude and direction. Your phone transmitting at high power can potentially interfere with and even damage these systems. So to be on the safe side, airlines actually require that all electronic devices be switched to airplane mode during takeoff, landing and all phases of flight. Every modern smartphone and tablet has an airplane mode that accomplishes 3 things. It turns off the cellular connection, it turns off the WiFi and Bluetooth radios, and it mutes all sounds and vibrations. This ensures that your device emits zero electromagnetic interference that could possibly mess with the plane's navigation and communication systems. Hope this helps! Signing off, LOKI
